source_text: Critiques of the evidence for UTI risk reduction emphasize potential confounders, such as selection bias in premature infants who face elevated UTI risks (3-8.5% versus 0.7-2% in term infants) from NICU interventions like catheterization and physiological immaturity, yet are typically deferred from neonatal circumcision due to instability; modeling suggests this confounding could account for a fourfold observed difference absent a genuine effect. [83]
